top_stories.title: Microsoft 365 accounts compromised at 79 organizations, no passwords needed
top_stories.summary: An attacker compromised Microsoft 365 accounts at 79 organizations over ten weeks by replaying stolen authentication sessions, bypassing password requirements entirely. Huntress researchers documented 497 successful sign-ins between July 14 and September 22, 2026, with sessions replayed from servers at 1337 Services GmbH, and attackers used hidden inbox rules to conceal their activity from victims.

top_stories.title: 1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents log in without ever seeing the password
top_stories.summary: 1Password launched "1Password for Agents," a sign-in platform enabling personal AI agents from Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI to authenticate to services without directly accessing passwords. The product addresses the emerging challenge of non-human identity and credential management for AI agents performing autonomous tasks.

top_stories.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — And Fraudsters Are Counting on It
top_stories.summary: The article addresses how threat actors are bypassing technical security controls by using AI-assisted social engineering against help desks to gain unauthorized access. This attack vector directly targets identity verification and authentication processes at service desks, a core concern for IAM and PAM professionals managing access requests.

top_stories.title: AI Agents as Insider Threats: Inside Microsoft's Bet on a Unified Security Stack
top_stories.summary: Microsoft's Project Perception introduces Guardian Agents designed to monitor and contain anomalous AI agent behavior within its security stack. The initiative raises questions about AI agent identity, authorization boundaries, and insider threat modeling as autonomous agents increasingly require IAM controls similar to human users.

top_stories.title: Tech Giants Block eMudhra Certificates Tied to 8 Compromised Keys
top_stories.summary: Google, Mozilla, Apple, and the Go project have blocked certificates from Indian certificate authority eMudhra after discovering 8 compromised cryptographic keys. The nature of the key compromise remains unclear, but the swift action by major tech platforms affects the trust chain for certificates issued by this CA.

news.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
news.summary: LiteLLM disclosed that a master key accidentally published to a public GitHub repository in late May 2026 was exploited by a threat actor to steal GitHub tokens and hijack the release pipeline. The attacker used the exposed key to push a malicious version of the LiteLLM Python package, compromising the software supply chain.

news.title: jumpserver v4.10.20
news.summary: JumpServer released version 4.10.20 of its open-source Privileged Access Management platform. The platform provides secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, database, and RemoteApp endpoints through a web browser for DevOps and IT teams.

news.title: Three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of Okta’s Oktane event
news.summary: TheCUBE's coverage of Okta's Oktane event highlighted key insights around AI agent governance and identity security. The coverage focused on how enterprises need identity controls that follow AI agent actions across applications beyond initial authentication.

news.title: Microsoft Teams to get AI-powered, context-aware phishing detection
news.summary: Microsoft announced plans to add AI-powered phishing detection to Microsoft Teams messages, with the feature expected to launch in early November 2026. The capability will analyze message context to identify phishing attempts within the Teams collaboration platform.

news.title: You gave your AI agent access, but who is giving it orders?
news.summary: Gen Digital has introduced an Agent Trust Hub designed to address security risks posed by AI agents that have been granted legitimate system permissions. The solution focuses on protecting AI agents from manipulation via malicious inputs by providing skill verification, secure connectivity, and runtime controls to intercept dangerous actions.

news.title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials
news.summary: A large-scale cyberattack campaign has breached enterprise firewalls and VPNs, exposing over 70,000 credentials by targeting Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect devices. Attackers gained access to numerous organizations worldwide and attempted further compromise of some victims.

news.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
news.summary: A webinar addresses the security risks posed by unmanaged AI agents operating within enterprise networks, which store API keys and database passwords while accessing internal systems without oversight or access reviews. The content focuses on how AI agents represent a new category of non-human identity and insider threat that falls outside traditional IAM governance frameworks.

news.title: Enable cross-Region fine-grained data access with AWS Lake Formation and Trusted Identity Propagation
news.summary: AWS has extended Trusted Identity Propagation with AWS IAM Identity Center to support cross-Region operations for Lake Formation-governed data. The feature enables fine-grained access control across Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift resources in different AWS Regions while preserving the actual corporate user identity throughout queries.

news.title: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
news.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed a supply chain compromise in LiteLLM version 1.107.0 that used Python startup hooks to steal credentials. The attack involved remote code loading mechanisms designed to exfiltrate credentials from affected systems.

news.title: Cybersecurity Stocks Rise as Evercore Survey Flags Strengthening Demand: Okta, CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Climb 4%
news.summary: Cybersecurity stocks including Okta rose approximately 4% following an Evercore ISI quarterly survey indicating strengthening demand in the sector. The stock movement reflects broader cybersecurity market sentiment rather than any Okta-specific product or business development.

news.title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
news.summary: Exaforce published an analysis of machine-speed cyberattacks involving stolen credentials, GitHub tokens, malicious AI installers, and MFA phishing campaigns. The report argues that automated detection and containment are necessary because attackers can steal credentials and begin exfiltrating data within minutes of compromise.

news.title: LiteLLM hit by second supply chain attack this year, users urged to rotate credentials
news.summary: LiteLLM suffered a second supply chain attack in 2026, with a malicious release pushed to PyPI and Docker registries designed to harvest cloud credentials, developer secrets, and API keys. The attack follows an earlier March compromise where a 153GB stolen archive was linked to 2,488 corporate domains including AWS, Samsung, Cisco, and Salesforce, with users now urged to rotate credentials.

news.title: eMudhra to Exit Global SSL/TLS Business After 8 Intermediate CA Keys Found Easily Guessable
news.summary: eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, announced it will exit its global SSL/TLS certificate business after a researcher discovered that private keys for eight of its intermediate CA certificates were easily guessable and recoverable. The company's board made the decision five days after the vulnerability was reported, and eMudhra stated it will replace affected customers' certificates with free ones from partners.

news.title: Railway Says Intruder May Have Accessed Customer Secrets, Urges Credential Rotation
news.summary: Railway, a Platform-as-a-Service provider, disclosed that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted customer environment variables, including decrypted contents in some cases. The company is urging credential rotation following the breach, which affected a subset of users.

news.title: OpenCode Flaw Lets Malicious MCP Servers Execute Code During Sign-In on Windows and WSL
news.summary: A vulnerability in the OpenCode AI coding agent allowed malicious MCP servers to execute arbitrary code on Windows or WSL systems during the sign-in process. The flaw, which caused injected code to run with the developer's own access privileges, was patched by Anomaly in version 1.18.33.

news.title: AGL hits half-million milestone with passkey adoption
news.summary: AGL has reached 500,000 passkey adoptions, marking a significant milestone in its consumer authentication initiative. The company discussed its technology stack and approach to authentication uplift as part of the rollout.

news.title: Keeper Security Launches AI-Powered Phishing Protection To Warn Users Before Entering Credentials on Fake Sites
news.summary: Keeper Security has launched an AI-powered phishing protection feature that detects look-alike domains, spoofed sites, and credential harvesting attempts before users enter passwords. The on-device AI capability is part of Keeper's zero-trust and zero-knowledge identity security platform.

news.title: authentik version/2026.8.5
news.summary: authentik has released version 2026.8.5 of its open-source identity provider and SSO platform. The release supports SAML, OAuth2/OIDC, LDAP, and RADIUS protocols for centralized authentication, authorization, and access management.

news.title: Enabling Passkeys Is Not the Same as Enforcing Them
news.summary: This article addresses the technical distinction between enabling and enforcing passkeys in Microsoft Entra ID, covering authentication strengths and Conditional Access policy design. It is part three of a seven-part series on migrating from MFA to passkeys in Entra ID, focusing on closing weak-fallback and device-code flow gaps.

news.title: Close Identity Gaps in Software Development Before Unleashing AI
news.summary: A Dark Reading roundtable examined how AI is creating identity security gaps in the software development lifecycle. CISOs discussed collaboration, improved identity visibility, and reduced testing costs as strategies to address these challenges.

news.title: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Backups Amid Concerns for Downstream MSPs
news.summary: ConnectWise disabled cloud backup functionality after researchers identified attackers authenticating into Microsoft 365 tenants using ConnectWise credentials. ConnectWise states customer impact remains unconfirmed while the incident raises concerns about credential-based access compromise affecting downstream managed service providers.

news.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Zero-Day Continues Trend of Exploited Edge Bugs
news.summary: BeyondTrust's Remote Support product was hit by a zero-day vulnerability, joining Ivanti, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks in a wave of exploited edge device bugs in the same week. BeyondTrust is a privileged access management (PAM) vendor, making this directly relevant to IAM security infrastructure.

news.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
news.summary: Microsoft released a patch update addressing more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software products. This patch batch exceeds the previous record of approximately 1,000 fixes issued in September.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch update addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. The company attributed the increased vulnerability discovery pace to AI tooling, while security experts noted organizations are struggling to keep up with testing and deploying the high volume of monthly patches.
